chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdul Aziz ibn Yahya said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammarah narrated to us from his father, from the Truthful (al-Sadiq) Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One of my own flesh and blood will be buried in the land of Khorasan. Any believer who visits him will be guaranteed Paradise by God, the Mighty and Majestic, and his body will be secured from the Fire.'

key_terms.أَرْضِ خُرَاسَانَ: The land of Khorasan (a historical region in Greater Iran)
key_terms.بَضْعَةٌ: A piece of flesh; a close relative or descendant
key_terms.حَرَّمَ جَسَدَهُ: He made his body forbidden (secure from)
key_terms.يَزُورُهَا: He visits it (referring to the shrine/grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the shrine in Khorasan mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, specifically identifies the 'descendant' buried in Khorasan as Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.), linking the prophetic promise to the shrine in Tus. It underscores the Shia theological concept of *ziyarat* as a means of securing salvation, where the physical act of visiting the Imam’s resting place serves as a tangible sign of faith that guarantees Paradise and liberation from the Fire.
